newsitem.title: CHINA: China says no big change in Deng Xiaoping's health.
newsitem.headline: China says no big change in Deng Xiaoping's health.

text.p: The health of China's 92-year-old leader Deng Xiaoping has not changed dramatically, a government spokesman said on Tuesday.
"There has been no big change," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a news briefing when asked about the health of the nation's paramount leader.
"For an old man, he is doing relatively well," Shen said. He declined further comment.

Deng, whose pragmatic policies helped transform China from a backward Stalinist state into an economic powerhouse, has not been seen in public in nearly two years. In his last appearance he looked frail and faltering.
Speculation abounds about his health, ranging from rumours he was admitted to hospital in recent days to reports he remains at home, although no longer mentally alert.

Deng had vowed to visit Hong Kong to witness the return of the British colony to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30 this year but a Beijing official believed to be close to the Deng family said recently this was unlikely.
